clean: Feature request for the export tool. Right now exports are limited to 100,000 rows, and our largest customers hit that limit every week. The current workaround is to split the export by date range, which is tedious and error prone. It would be much better if the tool could stream the results to a file and email a download link. I think we can reuse the background job system for this. The job would write to temporary storage, and the link would expire after seven days, since people may not check email right away. We should also add a progress indicator. I would estimate this at about a week of work, give or take.

clean: I need to prepare for a job interview next week for a project manager position. The company builds logistics software, and the interview has three rounds. Can you act as the interviewer and ask me behavioural questions, one at a time? After each answer, give me feedback on the structure and the clarity. If my answer is too long, tell me what to cut. Start with why I want this role. I want to practice the star format, which stands for situation, task, action and result.

Okay so I have been looking at the numbers for the last release and I want to share a few thoughts. The adoption of the new editor is lower than we expected, and I think part of the reason is that people do not know where to find it. We should probably just move the entry point to the main toolbar. The banner would help for a week or two, but after that it becomes noise. A permanent button is a better answer, and it costs us very little to build. The second thing I noticed is that the tutorial completion rate drops sharply at the third step. That step asks people to import, and a lot of them do not have one handy. So we could offer a sample file they can use to follow along. I can put together a mockup for both changes by the end of the day. Tell me if you think I am missing something obvious.

clean: Hey everyone, long post incoming, sorry in advance. I have been thinking about how we do planning, and I think we are making it harder than it needs to be. Every quarter we spent two weeks debating priorities, and then the priorities change in the first month anyway. I would rather we commit to a short list of things, and then decide the details as we go. I am not saying no planning, I am saying lighter planning, with a smaller list and a shorter meeting. The risk is that teams drift, so we would need a way to check in every few weeks. I actually think that is a feature, because it forces us to talk about what is working. If people are interested, I can write a one page proposal and we can try it next quarter. No pressure, I just wanted to put the idea out there.
